title: All Ancestors of a Node in a Directed Acyclic Graph
summary: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a list of directed edges, return for each node a sorted list of its ancestors, where an ancestor can be reached via a sequence of directed edges.
statement: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph with n nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, and a list of directed edges, return for each node a sorted list of its ancestors, where an ancestor can be reached via a sequence of directed edges.
constraints: Nodes are 0 through n-1 and the directed graph is acyclic.
An ancestor has a directed path of one or more edges to the node.
Return each node’s ancestors in increasing numeric order.
hints: A child inherits every ancestor of each parent, plus the parent itself.
Process parents before children with topological indegrees and propagate sets along outgoing edges.
Initialize zero-indegree nodes; for each edge update child set, decrement degree, and enqueue when ready.
DAG topological order guarantees every parent set is complete before its child is processed, so propagation finds every and only reachable predecessor.
editorial: DAG topological order guarantees every parent set is complete before its child is processed, so propagation finds every and only reachable predecessor.

tests.explanation: Propagating ancestor sets through topological order yields the eight requested sorted lists.
Node three has ancestors 0,1,2 and node four additionally includes three.
